paras: I got up at 4 a.m. and had everything packed and ready the night before: water bottles, and all the things I thought I wouldn't eat.
The ride starts at 6:00, and it was going to take me about 15 minutes to ride there, since I'm about 14 miles away. So I set out, light on my bike, early morning, jamming.
I get there and I'm nervous. Excited and nervous. There's not that many people there, maybe five or six in front of me, and I thought, oh no, they went to the wrong place.
Then within a couple minutes it just started filling up. It's a feeling of just go. You can tell people are ready to lock in and chat with their friends and ride their bikes.
It was cool. Fast paced, but manageable. Hockey, back and forth. I didn't even look down, really. I was so nervous I barely looked at my power or my speed or anything.
It started to cook up a little bit, and then I looked over and people are getting gels and eating. And I thought, okay, I know what that means. Something's about to happen.
We broke it out, let's talk about him. And return right on Dynamite, and motherfucker. Green, go. Smashed down. People just locked in.
You could see Cal from Bicycle Haüs lift his head, jockeying to see where people are. Finding Hudson. Curtis stuck his head up with this look of attack, but in a fun way. It was freaking awesome.

I tried to keep up with the pack. Everyone broke up into groups based on speed. I'm sure there are people who are super fast who stay in the back on purpose. Maybe they didn't feel good. Maybe they drank too much. Whatever.
I tried to keep up with the first group and I lost them. And I thought, you know what? Fuck it. I can get it. I can get it.
I was riding up, just pushing really hard. I couldn't do it, and then I kind of gassed a little bit.
Shana was back there behind me. She passed me with a group and she's just tapping on the shoulder. It's all good. You got this.
That was so nervous. I don't know. That was a pretty cool moment.

We get to the top of Dynamite, and I thought we were going to drink water. They were not. They just kept going. I followed them all the way to the roundabout, and I took off the gas a little bit and tried to relax, and I lost them. That's when I got lost up there.
I just ran around trying to find parts of the route. Sometimes I'd find it, and then I'd lose it.
I failed every part of that ride. I could have. And I can't tell you how much fun I had and how much I learned.
So that's that ride. It's fast. It's fun.

I also noticed two people, I'm like, I'm only gonna do half the writing, branched off and went and had coffee with their friends. It's what you wanted to be. But the moral of the story is, if you're looking for a good, fast paced ride, early morning, you're in Scottsdale. I say go for it.
